_comment: Per-row ceilings on the alpine/official ratio, enforced by
assert-perf-budgets.py. These are REGRESSION ALARMS, not parity targets:
the goal is <= 1.00, the budget is where a build has gone visibly wrong.
Seeded from three consecutive main runs (34257752564, 34269667105,
34276244690) at runs=1, plus perf-probe n=10 draws on three CPU models for
webkit. A ceiling is roughly the worst observed value plus 15%, because the
inline probe runs at n=1 where chromium's launch alone swung 0.69-1.51.
Rows that read exactly 1.00 in every run are budgeted tight (1.15). They are
frame-bound or JIT-bound and do not drift, which makes them the sharpest
detector we have: int_math read 5-9x when chromium shipped with DCHECKs on.
A row whose budget must be raised is a finding. Raise it in the same PR that
causes it, so the number moves where a reviewer can see it.
